No validated automated warfarin-dose implementation is provided by this application; a gene call alone is not a complete dosing recommendation. CPIC's warfarin guidance is a dosing algorithm rather than a recommendation for each genotype: "CPIC Guideline for Pharmacogenetics-Guided Warfarin Dosing: 2017 Update [Article: 28198005 ] recommends that pharmacogenetic warfarin dosing be accomplished through the use of one of the pharmacogenetic dosing algorithms, as summarized in Figure 2. See CPIC guideline annotation for details." That flow chart depends in part on ancestry, which this application does not collect, so rs12777823 is not assessed. The CYP2C9, VKORC1 and CYP4F2 results are shown for reference only.

interpretation: Phase 9 B10 added CYP2D6 outside calls (backend/app/outside_calls.py; pharmcat_runner, cpic_engine, coverage, main, models, explanation; the codeine capability), one codeine phrase in label_mapping.yaml, and the client's input and provenance; no supplied call is involved in the evaluation. Declared: the reworded codeine limitation in CYP2D6 eligibility and discrepancy detail (audit/phase9/B10_ZR_AMENDMENT.md). Its application rerun over the same 208 individuals reproduces every scored metric, exclusion and discrepancy of both the historical benchmark and the previous evaluation. Eligibility differs in the hash of each regenerated single-sample VCF (the path-bearing bcftools header) and in the changes declared in declared_eligibility_changes, and discrepancies differ only in the free-text detail declared in declared_discrepancy_detail_changes, each with its exact before and after value, row count and reason; against the historical benchmark they compose with earlier re-binds' declarations (cumulative_eligibility_changes); no scored metric, exclusion or discrepancy classification changed. No new genotype concordance or clinical claim follows.
